regime_context: The detector shows a textbook one-narrative regime for China A-shares: Banks rank #1 with extreme durability (0.87) and a crowding Z of 1.98 (crowded), in a 'trend' state; Coal is a distant challenger with a 'mean-revert' tag and weak breadth. Backtest verdict is explicit that the absolute-trend gate did NOT hold on this market and cross-sectional momentum rank-IC is ~0, so this is a focus/flow lens, not alpha — and the track record (dir_accuracy 0.337) warns against directional confidence.
emerging_watch: If Banks' durability_bar cools below ~0.7 and Coal's breadth widens above ~0.5 for 10 consecutive trading days, I would retire the one-narrative view and reassess Coal as a potential confirmed handoff — until then I treat Coal as a shallow challenger only.

theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks is the dominant, one-narrative theme with the highest score and the strongest trend-health leg (durability_bar 0.87, hurst 'trend', breadth 0.944). Its leadership is broad and cohesive, so if any theme holds in this tape, it is the most plausible candidate. The lean is a relative-tilt judgement, not a claim that the rank predicts returns — and the crowding flag (Z 1.98) is a size-down caution only, never a fade.
theses.dissent: Backtest verdict says the absolute-trend gate did not hold on this market (mean-reverting tape whipsaws the gate), and dir_accuracy of 0.337 suggests the detector's directional reads often miss; Banks could already be a late-cycle extension that mean-reverts.

falsifier.text: 512800.SS lags CSI 300 by 3% over any 20-day window even as its breadth stays above 0.8

theses.subject: Coal
theses.thesis: Coal is the only other eligible theme (eligible true, rank 2), but its trend-health leg is weak: durability_bar 0.47 with hurst 'mean-revert' and breadth just 0.2. The rotation breadth view is 'narrow' (2 of 22 eligible, frac 0.09), so this is not a confirmed handoff out of Banks — it is a shallow challenger in a one-narrative regime. Under the guardrails, flagging a confirmed handoff requires more evidence; Coal lacks the breadth/durability for that read yet.
theses.dissent: Coal's momentum score is strong enough to plausibly catch a short value rotation if macro risk appetite turns; avoiding it risks missing the only alternative leg in a market the gate failed to tame.
